speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Just when you become an expert in taking care of babies, they go to school, and it is a totally different challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And when you thought that you had finally mastered parenting school-going children, they become teenagers, and that presents another area of challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our children often do a better job at keeping up with the fast-changing world than parents do.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: By ensuring that they are so well taken care of, does it help them or are we inadvertently blunting their abilities to adapt?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Years ago, I taught my daughter how to cycle, and I learnt that a young girl cannot learn how to balance with an over-protective dad holding the back of the bicycle.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Eventually, when my running could not keep up with her pedalling, I did, and off she went.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: She learnt how to cycle, and I learnt how to let go.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Perhaps one of the best things we, as parents, can do for our children is to know when to let go and what to let go of.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But this does not mean that they will be left alone; they will have the love of the family, as well as support of the entire school system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is why parenthood is a roller coaster ride and for the lion-hearted.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But children need the time and space to explore in order to discover their strengths and their interests, find their place in the world and ignite their joy of learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is not just a matter of personal freedoms, but a pragmatic response to the fast changes in the world around us, a world where it is hard to identify the landing points that the unfolding story of the rise of China and technological advancement will lead us, a world where the young are creating their own jobs through startups and innovations and shaping their own future.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This requires us to give students a say in what, how and when they want to learn, to help them develop, discover and deepen their knowledge and skills in the areas that they are passionate about.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is the most precious gift for our children.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we cannot give it to them; we can only set them on a journey to discover it for themselves.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, both Minister Ng Chee Meng and Minister Ong Ye Kung spoke about preparing our children for a changing future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It is our goal to provide every child with the opportunity to get a good start in life, discover his strengths and interests, and help him realise his potential.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As we prepare our children to be future-ready, we want them to develop holistically.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We want to cater to the diverse interests of our students with multiple pathways and different options.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I know, as a father of two children, we all share the same goal – we want the best for our children and to bring out the best in them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: That is why we must work together, as strong school-home-community partnerships will lead to better student outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Over the years, we have made significant efforts and progress in building enduring partnerships with parents, the community and industry partners to support our schools and students, and we will continue to build upon these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together with the teachers in schools, they are crucial in supporting our children in discovering their strengths and achieving their aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This includes our efforts in exposing our children to a broad range of diverse sports, and developing those with sporting talent, which was raised by Mr Edwin Tong.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As Minister Ng shared, we have put in place various programmes to expose and nurture our students in this area.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I am glad that many parents and community partners also recognise the value of sports being inculcated in our young and partner schools to provide our children with the opportunities to try out different games and sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: If you were to visit Lianhua Primary School on a Saturday morning, you will see it bustling with energy, with students playing soccer in the field, while others play tennis in the sports hall.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These are, however, not school-based programmes but community programmes led by professional football club, Warriors Football Club (FC), as well as SC Global and Singapore Tennis Association.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Parents see to the logistics, take attendance and contribute in ways to ensure a smooth running of the programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Such partnerships augment schools' programmes, offer our students more options and expose them to a wider range of sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We also recognise the importance of bringing together community and industry partners whose expertise and resources can extend the knowledge and learning in schools through authentic contexts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is particularly relevant in the learning of our MTLs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For instance, the teaching of the Malay Language does not just belong to the cikgu or the parents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It also involves the Malay community coming together to deepen our students' sense of their own culture and rich heritage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Perkasa Warisan Camp designed for our Primary 4 students is one such initiative.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Allow me to elaborate more about the camp in Malay.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Themed Malay Gastronomy, our students will learn about indigenous herbs and spices in the outdoors before applying that knowledge to create their own unique nutritious salad dish and share their ideas with their peers and parents in a creative way.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One of our teachers whose expertise was tapped on to design the learning experiences of the camp is Mr Azhar Bin Abdul Rashid.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We hope to extend this initiative to more schools in other GRCs in the future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In English): For our younger children at the preschool level, we want to spark their interest in learning Malay through play.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Such collaborations are made possible as the Malay Language Learning and Promotion Committee has established a good system to facilitate networking and partnerships among schools, preschools, community organisations, such as the Malay Youth Literary Association (4PM) and ASAS '50 (The Singapore Writers' Movement ’50), and Government agencies, including the People's Association (PA), National Library Board (NLB), NParks, National Heritage Board (NHB) and the National Arts Council (NAC).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chen Show Mao asked if we can also extend the learning of Malay language to other students at the primary level, by including conversational Malay language skills as part of schools' formal curriculum.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Conversational Malay Programme was introduced since 2005, where non-Malay students learn to conduct simple conversations in the Malay language and gain appreciation of the Malay culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This equips our students with some grounding of the Malay language so that they can pick up the language more easily should they need it for economic or other reasons in their adult lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Lastly, let us talk about the industry, how we can partner them to complement and supplement our students’ learning in schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is what Applied Learning is all about, where our students learn by doing and experience the real-world application of sustainable farming.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These are small but important steps in guiding our students to care for others and contribute to the community within their means.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: However, as the Malay saying goes, "Sedikit-sedikit, lama-lama jadi bukit, sehari selembar benang, lama-lama menjadi kain", meaning a little effort in time makes a hill, and a thread woven becomes a cloth.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I believe we can go a lot further and do a lot more for our students when we do it hand in hand with our parents, community and industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together, we play a collaborative role in preparing our next generation to be ready for the new world.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Ng Chee Meng, Minister Ong Ye Kung, Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Faishal Ibrahim have expounded on the shifts we are making in our education landscape to better equip Singaporeans for the future economy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As we build up our people’s skills, competency in our MTLs is an important area that will stand Singaporeans in good stead.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to continue in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Bilingualism has always been an integral part of our education policy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With the increasingly interconnected global landscape, proficiency in our MTLs and cultural heritage will also help us to connect with our global partners more effectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked about our efforts to enhance our students' proficiency in MTLs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, our schools are instrumental in providing a nurturing environment for students to learn and explore their MTLs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With the support of the three MTL Promotion Committees and Lee Kuan Yew Fund for Bilingualism, local arts and cultural groups, media as well as grassroots organisations, our schools have been incorporating various creative ways to express the languages, including xinyao, comic writing, radio drama writing, community tours and even games, in their teaching of MTLs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, teachers in Jing Shan Primary School developed a platform called "Story Village" that lets students improve their Chinese through interactive games and interesting stories.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The more proficient learners can even help their friends learn the language by creating new game software in Chinese.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through such innovative MTL teaching, we hope that the learning of MTLs becomes a part of the students' everyday life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MTL is not just a subject, it is a live language.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Minister Ng Chee Meng has mentioned, real-life applications can help make the MTLs come alive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Hence, we seek to cultivate students’ interest to continue learning and using their MTLs by ensuring that MTL learning is engaging and relevant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Second, we hope to create a vibrant and supportive environment for MTL learning beyond schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We encourage parents to use MTL with their children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This can involve day-to-day activities, such as watching a show or movie, listening to songs or reading a book in their MTL with the children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will also provide parents with various resources to support their teaching of MTL to their children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One example is the Annual MTL Symposium (MTLS), which brings together many experts and specialists to share tips and resources with parents on the teaching of MTLs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year, more than 15,000 parents, educators and students participated in and benefited from this symposium.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, parents can use the interactive iMTL portal with their children at home to help and guide their children to learn and practise MTLs at their own pace.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our local arts and cultural groups, media as well as grassroots organisations can also provide rich contexts to excite our students to use their MTLs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, the Indian Heritage Centre worked with the Tamil Language Learning and Promotion Committee to develop a Discovery Kit that lets students practise the language as they explore the centre.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Like the learning of many skills today, Members have heard from the Ministers, the Senior Minister of State, the Senior Parliamentary Secretary the learning of our MTLs does not stop after we leave school.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides strengthening our proficiency in MTLs, what are the other work-relevant skills that we need to develop to face and thrive in the future economy?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is really what the SkillsFuture is all about.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And Members have heard Minister Ong Ye Kung talking about it earlier.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree with Assoc Prof Randolph Tan that literacy and ICT skills are critical skills for our workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is why our Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) framework includes Workplace Literacy and Numeracy as well as International Computing Driving Licence courses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: ICT is also the top area of training that is supported by SkillsFuture Credit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Dr Intan Mokhtar asked about the impact of the SkillsFuture movement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: According to the WSQ Outcomes Evaluation Survey 2016, 90% of respondents indicated that their WSQ training has helped them work more effectively and more efficiently, and 72% found that it had facilitated their job search.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Nonetheless, some Singaporeans may need help to navigate the training landscape, as Dr Intan Mokhtar has pointed out.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our schools and IHLs have strengthened their Education and Career Guidance efforts to help students better appreciate the strengths and passions that they possess, and also better understand the available education and career opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This information transparency spurs the PEIs to keep their programmes industry-relevant and graduates' skills employable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To encourage and facilitate our people's training journey, we have tailored and personalised the MySkillsFuture portal to meet individual training needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This portal allows users to access industry information and search for jobs and training opportunities according to their interests.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: On this website, we also highlight exemplary employers who are avid supporters of staff training.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To broaden our public outreach, we have partnered our five Community Development Councils to introduce SkillsFuture Advice workshops to help Singaporeans understand work trends and workplace skills needed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through the SkillsFuture Advice workshop, she became more aware of her own training needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: She now actively uses the MySkillsFuture portal to search for leadership and management courses to improve her work as a director.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Minister Ong Ye Kung had mentioned, we will continue to expand the learning options for Singaporeans and that includes working with IHLs to introduce more courses for adult learners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Part of this will involve resourcing IHLs with the best talents, local and foreign, for teaching and research.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about the local representation in our AUs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Together with our parents and partners, we will continue to strive to equip and empower Singaporeans in their lifelong learning journey ahead so that we can all gear up to seize the opportunities in the future.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: To the Senior Minister of State, who could have been distracted by Member Leon Perera's suggestion to have MPs help conduct political education in schools, but this is not about that.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: The feedback is that the resources are insufficient and the model is quite inadequate.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, I seek the Senior Minister of State's consideration for that.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: The second clarification is also my second time request for a SPED Academy to place more strategic priority and focus so that we can create lifelong learners as well out of the special needs population, just like NUS adopting its alumni now and looking at their graduates over a 20-year timeframe.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I wonder if we could do the same for SPED.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: The next clarification is addressed to the two Ministers.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: It sounds like MOE has got its act altogether and that you have covered all grounds.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I was just wondering, in a future that is constantly disrupted and at most times unpredictable, how do you navigate a space like this to ensure more learner agility amongst our students and even more self-directed learning from a very young age?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Indeed, we want to strengthen support, but the question is how.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think Ms Denise Phua and many others will appreciate that the SPED space is not homogenous, with very varied challenges, very varied needs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: When I describe things like the structures that we have or the 80% of students with SENs in our mainstream schools, that is not a model.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: That is an outcome of the approach that we are taking.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We currently have a space with a wide variety of service delivery models and a wide variety of structures.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we have to take a little bit of a step back and have a sense that there really is no clear single answer about a single best model.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But there are some common challenges that we need to address in terms of strengthening our support.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: That is the biggest single focus of the work that we are doing.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the answer to the Member's first question is yes.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is no single model of SPED delivery and we are quite open to studying further models.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As a system, we remain open-minded, as open-minded as possible, not to be blindsided by different trends that may surface.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Some trends would be relevant, some trends may fade.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Structurally, we do reviews in MOE periodically across all different subjects and we do benchmarking with renowned institutions around the world and we also go on study visits.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: My staff actually asked me, "What would you like to learn in Australia?" I wanted to look at outdoor education and how it would strengthen a perceived weakness in our own system.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, we look at different systems to learn new things.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We also have research and development (R&D) arms set up in NIE and MOE.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: These research entities plug into the world institutions where they do research on pedagogical, heutagogical or andragogical updates.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We are always trying to keep at the forefront of developments.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But always, as I said earlier, remembering to customise it to our Singapore context.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Chairman, a short reply to Ms Denise Phua because she asked the Ministers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The short answer is help the students find what they love to do.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If it is something they love to do, they will be self-directed and they will learn their whole life.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The first is addressed to Minister Ng Chee Meng.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: So, I would like the Minister's response to that.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The second clarification is directed to Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling on the composition of local academics in context-sensitive faculties in our local universities.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Is there a need, is there a deliberate attempt to increase this composition or number?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: To assist our students from lower socio-economic backgrounds, this is always a work-in-progress.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We will do our best, but it will never be an ending where we will be happy with it.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: You can see from the different programmes that we have started.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: When we started the kindergartens, we wanted to address these disadvantages and bring disadvantaged students to as equal a starting line as possible.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I have said in my speech the different levelling up of criteria, including for Edusave.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We also, in our schools, pay very, very high attention to learning support programmes for students coming into our primary schools at Primary 1.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: If they are slower, whether in the languages, in English or in Mathematics, we have different programmes to support them in Primary 1 and Primary 2, and we extend it all the way to Primary 6 if required.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Most of the kids do well and they graduate from these support programmes by the time they are at Primary 3.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It is almost like a relax area where a VWO person or teacher stays back to supervise them.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: They get to hang out in a cool room where there is play but only after they have done their homework part.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I have my own experience through the family support services where we also partner Family Service Centres (FSCs).

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Children from lower socio-economic backgrounds may not have a conducive home environment.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We partner the community services to make sure that they are well looked after and well-supervised so that they are not distracted.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But there are ground realities that we have to cope with, such as family circumstances, even family abuse.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: All these are difficult entrenched problems that we face.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Our teachers even tell me sometimes that they wake up earlier in the morning and go to the flat of the students to bring them to school.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But on the Member's question, I fully agree with him that all our universities are national universities.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They must understand local issues, Singapore's and our region's challenges and they must understand the context of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Faculty who understand the context of Singapore can be locals and can be foreigners.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So long as they understand the context and they do research and teaching that are within that context, we welcome them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Having said that, we do want to develop local scholars who will rise up through the ranks.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: He did not directly reply to me; so, again, I would just like to ask him if he could directly reply to confirm that point.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I cited some facts that would seem to suggest that that is the case, but I am not sure.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, I am not making any assertion, I am just posing a question.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Was it the case in the past that MPs could attend events in schools in their MP capacity and, if so, why was that then not deemed to be partisan politics?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The third question is linked to the first two: if that was the case, then when was this policy changed, and why was it changed at the time it was changed?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Lastly, I am just going to take another crack at this.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: If Ministers and GRAs can attend events in schools and interact with students as Ministers and GRAs, following a certain set of rules and that is not deemed to be partisan, why cannot Members of this House from other parties and also NMPs similarly interact with students following exactly the same rules?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Why would the one set of interactions be deemed to be inherently and by definition non-partisan, the other inherently and by definition partisan?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Has he attended a school and interacted with students?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I alluded to that in my cut speech.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I attended one event in my private sector capacity.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And in that capacity, I only spoke about one aspect of my private sector work, did not touch on anything to do with my role as an MP or perspectives on current affairs, public matters and so on.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Perera is clear that he is able to separate out his partisan political views from attending and interacting with people in other capacities.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, that is the answer to Question 4.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: All kinds of people can have political views.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: People who drive buses, people who prepare our food, our teachers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But you have to be very clear about the role in which one attends and interacts with students.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And that is the basis for the first question.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: People do attend, and they do so in a very clear capacity that is non-partisan in nature.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In the past, the policy was the same.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the specific instance that the Member referred to, I believe, does not actually specify the capacity in which the person was speaking at the school or meeting the school.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It was those years in his capacity as an MP.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, my reading of the exact same text that he has quoted is that what was referenced was the time in years that he had spent as an MP, not that he was attending the school in his capacity as an MP.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think that point is really quite clear if one reads the text properly and is not seeking a derived meaning from it.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Perera, I have to call Miss Cheng Li Hui first.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: It is sometimes hard for parents of special needs children to find preschools that are willing to take in their children.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: For example, we have some special needs children in my PAP Community Foundation (PCF) centres in Tampines, but they are no longer Tampines residents.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: They have moved out but when they moved to a new estate, they have problems finding another preschool which is willing to take in their children.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Since MK is extending to more estates, can MK play a bigger role in this?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: After checking with some teachers, they say that MK does not have enough special needs programmes as well.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: So, can the Minister just clarify on this?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: I also have another question that is a bit more for the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), but it is about preschools.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Can there be more funding and training for teachers who care for and teach special needs children?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Because they have some problems in terms of the timing as the core curriculum is only four hours, but the DSP programme comes in during the four hours and takes the children out for one hour.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: The teachers feel that they can actually do that after-hours.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Leon Perera, do you want to clarify?

speaker: The Chairman
text: We do not want to go into a debate on this issue.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Just to clarify the answer that the hon Senior Minister of State gave.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I have come across websites of schools which have chronologies of past events where the events describe an MP attending in their MP capacity before 2011 or thereabouts, and the grassroots adviser attending after 2011 or so.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, in the context of this sort of information, I would just like to confirm again ‒ and this is really my last point ‒ is it the case that that has always been the policy that MPs cannot attend in their MP capacity and only in their grassroots adviser capacity?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: When I go to visit the Singapore Armed Forces Reservists Association (SAFRA), which I have done recently, on the banner, it said that "Visit by Dr Janil Puthucheary".

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I was not there in my medical capacity.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Chairman, I would like to address this to the Minister for Education (Schools).

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Can I clarify that, together with that, there will also be a review of the textbooks and activity books used in the primary schools because, at this point in time, as a parent, I can share with you feedback that there is too much repetitive and rote learning in our activity books and worksheets given to students?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: So, in order to ensure that there is applied learning done in schools, I think there should be a lot more practice where the skills are learnt in a contextual manner.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We will continue with this process to make sure our teaching materials are properly updated.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Alright, if there are no further clarifications, would Ms Denise Phua like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Mr Chairman, Nelson Mandela once said that education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, on behalf of all my colleagues here, I would like to thank the entire MOE team ‒ the support staff must be somewhere around in the building ‒ for helping us to change the world for the better for all of our students, families and professionals.
